seal.statement: The seven-node in-process cold-formation probe's cross-owner harness model is derived from the registered owner contracts rather than hand-maintained: a model module enumerates every registered coupled pair and contract as a driver-host that hosts the real production owner with its drive methods sealed, every registered invariant owner is a hosted owner, the hand-wired stand-in family in the membership-consistency helpers is replaced by those hosts, and a test derived from the registry fails whenever a registered interaction is absent from the model, so the model can no longer go stale without the gate saying so.

text: Derived harness model landed in test/distributed/harness/owner-interaction-model.js: hostedInteractions(root) builds one host per registered coupled pair and per contract with src/ owners, consuming the registry's own owner records (exact module, stem-prefix, directory scope) rather than re-classifying paths; a host imports its real owner modules, seals every exported function (create() throws on an override for a sealed name, the driver-host shape), records directory owners as scopes without loading them, and hostedOwnerKeys(root) maps each invariant to a host through its contractRef. Test made async to await the model; the three shard manifests regenerated for the new test file. Receipts: registered-interactions-all-hosted and hosts-are-real-owners-with-sealed-drive pass; invariant-owners-hosted and stand-in-family-removed remain red.

26 of the 32 registered invariants cite a contractRef that is not a registry contract (CL-001, CL-033..CL-042, core-system-logic.md, publication-readiness-churn-liveness-closure.md, readiness-handoff-liveness.md, rolling-restart-rebalancer-handoff.md, golden-capability-gold-plating.md), across 9 of the 11 invariant owners; only active-gate-convergence binds. Derived hosting can therefore witness 6 invariants. The receipt invariant-owners-hosted stays red on this until an owner decides: register those contracts in test/shards/impact-contracts.json with owners and witness tests (widening this quest into the registry), or supersede the sealed receipt with one that hosts only registry-bound invariants and routes the unregistered 26 to a contracts-registration quest. Not decided here.

invariant-owners-hosted needs an owner decision: register the 26 invariants' contracts in the registry, or supersede the receipt to registry-bound invariants; the stand-in replacement (receipt 4) proceeds regardless.

Shape of the stand-in replacement (receipt 4). The six stand-ins in membership-consistency-integration-test-helpers.js exist to make CDC propagation SLOW and observable between two caches (createRealisticCDCService: setTimeout-delayed applySystemTableChange on target caches) and to give RebalanceCoordinator/gateway/readiness hand-built collaborators. The real CDC owner (src/cdc/cdc-integration-service-*.js) has no time seam: it reaches ambient setTimeout in cache-visibility-wait, authoritative-catchup and shared. So a driver-host for the CDC hop on the deterministic convergence scheduler (test/convergence/deterministic-convergence-harness.js: schedule/runUntilIdle on a virtual clock) needs the owner to take an injected time source - a src/ change under the epic's authorizes, behind an independent verifier - after which the six stand-ins become hosts: real SystemTableCache pairs joined by the real CDC owner on virtual time, real RebalanceCoordinator/ControlPlaneSystemTableGateway/ControlPlaneReadinessService constructed through ControlPlaneSetup with those collaborators. This is also the seam formation-sim needs (virtual clock, cost model), so it is done once here.

Owner decision (2026-09-12): receipt invariant-owners-hosted is superseded (R09) from 'every invariant owner is hosted' to 'every registry-bound invariant is hosted and every unbound citation is named' - the derived model now reports each unbound citation with its invariant id and formation-contracts-registration (inserted before formation-sim) drives that number to zero by registering each with one witness or retiring it. The CDC time seam is authorized as this quest's first src/ change; src/cdc widened into the epic's authorizes for that owner only; seam shape from message-group-service-raft-timing.js.

CDC time seam (first src/ change, authorized 2026-09-12): CDCIntegrationService resolves this.timeSource = resolveTimeSource(options) in its constructor, the same collapse helper every seamed owner uses (src/time/time-source.js); the cache-visibility wait arms and clears its timeout on it, the shared delay becomes delayOn(timeSource, ms) and both retry-delay sites in the routed-mutation readiness and the visibility wait's authoritative-fallback delay arm on this.timeSource, and the authoritative catch-up's default sleep/now read resolveTimeSource(service) so a bare service record still gets the platform clock byte-for-byte. No ambient setTimeout remains in the service modules (cdc-confirmation-tracker.js keeps its own timer; it is not constructed by the service and is outside this seam). Witness test/cdc/cdc-integration-service-time-seam.test.js: 3 pass with the seam, 0/3 on revert; the owner's existing 170 tests pass. Shard manifests regenerated for the new test. Awaiting independent verification before landing (epic guardrail).

Category-complete adversarial round against sweep-timer, retry-loops and harness-fidelity. REJECT. retry-loops: the routed-mutation retry loop is split across two clocks - waitForRetryBudget and the remainingBudgetMs exit read Date.now() (cdc-routed-mutation-readiness.js:433,436,521) while the inter-attempt delay reads this.timeSource; verifier probe shows 6/4/1 attempts and per-attempt timeoutMs depending on the wall clock under a virtual one. sweep-timer: the cache-visibility wait's budget is ambient - createTimeoutBudget at cache-visibility-wait.js:141 takes no now, and getRemainingBudgetMs at :334 passes this.now which the service does not define, so it falls to Date.now; remaining budget is ~1000 not ~250 when the virtual timer fires. harness-fidelity: the seamed fallback delay, both retry-delay sites and the catch-up default sleep/now are exercised by no test on a virtual clock (null-engine fixture returns deferred_by_pressure before the delay; catch-up tests always inject sleep); test 2's red-on-revert is a missing-export TypeError, not a behavioural failure; test 3 does not assert RealTimeSource. out-of-bar:data-timestamps: insert normalization and the node-joined event stamp wall-clock row values. Confirmed sound: cleanup clears on the same captured source on every path; catch-up receivers are always real services in production; confirmation tracker has no constructor site; 173/173 tests, eslint clean, diff byte-identical to the patch.

Corrective attempt answering cdc-time-seam-review-1. retry-loops: the routed-mutation loop's budget now reads the clock its delays arm on - queryExecutionDeadlineMs is set from and compared against this.timeSource.now() (cdc-routed-mutation-readiness.js), so attempt count and per-attempt timeout are a function of one clock. sweep-timer: the cache-visibility wait creates its timeout budget with now: () => timeSource.now() (clock captured before the executor, so the closure rule holds) and confirmCacheVisibilityHoleWithinBudget reads remaining budget with now: () => this.timeSource.now() instead of the undefined this.now. harness-fidelity: the witness file is rewritten from the verifier's own probes - the routed-mutation retry loop is driven by an engine returning deferred-retry failures and asserts the per-attempt timeout decays 200/150/100/50 with attempts spaced 0/50/100/150 in virtual time, settled by the virtual pump alone; the catch-up default sleep is driven through the real service with executeAuthoritativeSystemTableRead deferring three times, asserting 3 reads, 2 sleeps armed on the injected clock and the table recorded as failed; the default is asserted instanceof RealTimeSource; the shared-delay import test is gone. Red on revert is behavioural for all four (0/4: 'must be armed on the injected clock', 'must settle by virtual time alone'). Owner tests 170/170. out-of-bar:data-timestamps recorded as a finding: row timestamps (insert normalization, node-joined event) are HLC/data values owned elsewhere and are outside this seam. Remaining ambient Date.now() reads in the owner are metric durations only.

out-of-bar:data-timestamps - applyTimestampDefaults/applyTableInsertDefaults (cdc insert normalization) and the node-joined event stamp wall-clock row values; under the harness rows carry wall time while the owner's timers run on virtual time. These are data values (created_at/updated_at, event timestamps) owned by the HLC/insert-normalization path, not timers; whether formation-sim needs them virtual is a formation-sim decision, recorded here so it is not rediscovered.

Round 2, category-complete against sweep-timer, retry-loops, harness-fidelity. REJECT on one defect: the wait's timeout-error budget classification is still read on the ambient clock - cache-visibility-wait.js:247-252 calls createTimeoutBudgetError({budget: timeoutBudget}) without now, so remainingBudgetMs/boundaryHit (hence CACHE_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT vs EXACT_BOUNDARY_HIT, consumed by shared.js:601 and managed-split-retry-policy.js:60) are computed against Date.now while deadlineMs is on the virtual clock (probe: remainingBudgetMs 600 on a thrown timeout, 0 where the seam value is 250). harness-fidelity gap: the seamed fallback retry delay at :340 and the remaining-budget read at :335 have no virtual-clock witness (the null-engine repair leg returns deferred_by_pressure before them). Round-1 (a) confirmed answered: the routed-mutation loop is wall-clock-invariant under real, frozen, racing and backwards walls (attempts=4, timeouts 200/150/100/50 at virtual 0/50/100/150). Red on revert behavioural for all four witnesses; 174/174 tests; eslint clean; diff byte-identical before and after the verifier's revert cycle. out-of-bar: retry-exhaustion-typing (pre-existing: budget exhaustion inside waitForRetryBudget rethrows the engine failure rather than the typed exhaustion) and data-timestamps carried forward.

Corrective attempt answering cdc-time-seam-review-2. sweep-timer: the wait's timeout error now classifies its budget on the injected clock - createTimeoutBudgetError at the throw site receives now: () => timeSource.now(), so remainingBudgetMs/boundaryHit (and the CACHE_VISIBILITY_TIMEOUT vs EXACT_BOUNDARY_HIT decision consumers branch on) read the clock the deadline was stamped on. harness-fidelity: new witness drives the wait's own authoritative-fallback retry through a repair leg that neither confirms nor defers, asserting the fallback delay (authoritativeFallbackRetryDelayMs) is armed on the injected clock and that the thrown error's timeoutClassification.remainingBudgetMs equals the budget minus virtual now. 5/5 witnesses, 0/5 on revert, owner tests 170/170, eslint clean, diff byte-identical after the revert cycle.

Round 3, category-complete. REJECT on one new defect, found by probe: cdc-integration-service-authoritative-catchup.js:161 moved the catch-up now default onto the service clock, but that value is the readStartedAtMs DATA STAMP fed to evictOlderThanMs and authoritativeReadStartedAtMs, compared against updated_at and tombstone deletedAtMs which the cache stamps with Date.now; under a default VirtualTimeSource the anti-entropy sweep is inert (rowsSwept 0 vs 1) and completeObservationWriteIsFenced fences every tombstoned key. Fix named: keep now defaulting to Date.now (only the sleep needed the seam; no loop budget reads it). Round-2 defect confirmed closed: the error classification is identical under frozen, racing, behind and real wall clocks (timer at 750, error at 800, remaining 200, boundaryHit false); a partial revert of only that line fails only witness 2 at the remaining-budget assertion. harness-fidelity gap: no witness drives the leader-witnessed catch-up sweep on the virtual clock. Preferences: witness 2's pseudo-state 'unconfirmed' and a comment that reads 775 where the pump lands at 800. out-of-bar: sql-engine-clock, timer-unref (pre-existing), shard-census (three shard manifests also carry the parent quest's test - land scope). 175/175, eslint clean, diff byte-identical.

Corrective attempt answering cdc-time-seam-review-3. sweep-timer: the catch-up's now default returns to Date.now - it stamps readStartedAtMs, a data value the sweep compares against row updated_at and tombstone times the cache stamps on the wall clock; only the sleep is a timer and only the sleep stays on the service clock (comment at the site says why). harness-fidelity: new witness from the verifier's sweep probe - a stale wall-stamped row under a default VirtualTimeSource is swept (rowsSwept 1, row gone) with the virtual clock never moving; this one is a guard against the round-3 defect rather than a red-on-revert witness (pre-seam code also stamps on Date.now), and is described as such. Witness 2's stub uses visibilityState null instead of a pseudo-state and its comment now says the pump lands the 25ms delay one 50ms step later. 6/6 witnesses; on full revert 5 fail behaviourally and the sweep guard passes as expected; owner tests 170/170; eslint clean; diff byte-identical after the revert cycle.

Round 4, category-complete against sweep-timer, retry-loops, harness-fidelity. APPROVE. Every timer the owner arms is on the injected source (wait.js:158/:296/:344, routed.js:456/:467, catchup.js:164, shared.js:150) and every loop budget reads it (wait.js:148/:255/:339, routed.js:436/:439); data stamps stay on the wall clock (readStartedAtMs, created_at/updated_at, event timestamps) and no comparison reads two clocks; the round-3 sweep probe now prints rowsSwept 1 / stillCached false under real, virtual-0, virtual+now and virtual-wall clocks, and the tombstone fence no longer fences under a default virtual clock, while a simulation of the round-3 stamp still reproduces the defect (the guard discriminates). No production caller passes now to the catch-up. Full revert: 5/6 fail behaviourally on the named seam assertions, the sweep guard passes as declared; reapplied diff byte-identical. 176/176 tests; eslint clean; the three mixin hosts used by other tests still run 172/172. Findings (no defects): out-of-bar timer-unref (pre-existing), shard-census (manifests also carry the parent quest's test; regenerate at land), gateway-now (the gateway's authoritativeReadStartedAtMs must stay on the wall clock if it is ever seamed), sql-engine-clock (engine boundary); preference: the test header's 'red on revert' could note witness 5 is a guard.

Formatting-only delta after cdc-time-seam-review-4, forced by the pre-commit file-size ratchet: cdc-integration-service-cache-visibility-wait.js reached 800 lines by wc (the ratchet counts split-newline length, one more) and the source oversized count read 28/27. Round 4 re-issue on the formatting-only delta. APPROVE. The diff-of-diffs against the approved copy shows exactly three deltas in cache-visibility-wait.js - two removed comments and the delayOn call re-wrapped from four lines to two - and a token-level comparison with comments stripped finds no code change; the rebase left src/cdc and test/cdc byte-identical to their pre-rebase content (git diff --stat 6ef462a15 HEAD -- src/cdc test/cdc empty). All eighteen round-4 template verdicts hold with the same evidence; the round-3 sweep and fence probes reproduce the healthy result on four clocks and the defect on the simulation; the revert cycle on cd5961a9a gives 5 fail / 1 pass with the same named mechanisms and reapplies byte-identical; 348/348 across the six affected test files; eslint clean. Findings carried forward (no defects): timer-unref, shard-census, gateway-now, sql-engine-clock, the test-header wording; new preference: the two removed comments were the only in-file statement that budget and timer read one clock.

Altitude check before receipt 4 (stand-in-family-removed). What the six stand-ins are for: createRealisticCDCService fakes CDC propagation between two SystemTableCaches with setTimeout; createMockMessageRouter, createMockRebalanceCoordinator, createMockTablePolicyService, createCacheControlPlaneGateway and createCacheBackedReadinessService hand the RebalanceCoordinator/gateway/readiness roles to hand-built objects; MockMessageGroupService stands in for a follower replica, with a note in the test saying a real follower would need a multi-node cluster. The honest hosting now exists: test/distributed/harness/virtual-network.js registers N nodes with per-node TimeSource adapters (networkTimeSource) and delivers messages with seeded delay on one virtual clock, and the CDC owner now takes that time source (seam approved, review-4-reissue). So the CDC hop host is: two nodes on a VirtualNetwork, each with a real SystemTableCache and a real CDCIntegrationService on networkTimeSource(node), the leader's cache mutation emitted as a network message whose follower handler is the real replication apply (MessageGroupService.applyCDCEvent -> cache); waitForPropagation is network.run(); the follower replica the note says is out of scope is a real node on the network. The gateway and readiness hosts are the real ControlPlaneSystemTableGateway (cache read path, no SQL engine) and the real ControlPlaneReadinessService over the same cache and CDC owner; TablePolicyService, StorageAdmissionService and StorageCapacityAccountingService are real classes taking cache+gateway; RebalanceCoordinator is real through ControlPlaneSetup wiring. The one surface that is not honestly hostable without a cluster is sqlQueryEngine: five subtests hand cdcService.sqlQueryEngine (today a stub returning success/empty rows) to the coordinator/readiness stand-ins, and the real coordinator routes writes through it. Judgment needed on which of two shapes this quest takes: (A) a real SQLQueryEngine over in-memory PartitionServices per node (what the seven-node probe does; heavy but real), or (B) treat the SQL engine as a transport-level seam like the virtual network - a harness-owned engine that applies writes to the node's cache with network delay - and record it in the model as a scope, not a stand-in. A rewrites the 14-subtest, 1300-line integration test around real partitions; B keeps the test's cache-level purpose and is one host module plus a helper rewrite. Neither is decided here.

Owner decision (2026-09-12) on the receipt-4 altitude check: shape B with a contract attached. The membership-consistency test proves cache-level membership consistency; a real SQL engine over per-node partitions inside it buys no new proof of that property and duplicates the seven-node probe. Three conditions: (1) the SQL-engine <-> cache/membership interaction is a REGISTERED coupled pair, so the derived model lists it as seamed-here, real-there with a pointer to the test that runs the real engine, and a dangling pointer turns the harness receipt red - the same mechanism as the unbound citations; (2) the stand-in is contract-bound: the engine's contract is one test suite run twice, against the real SQLQueryEngine and against the seam, so a behaviour change fails both or fails the seam's conformance run; (3) the model records where the engine is real - the seven-node probe - because routed system-table reads are on the starvation path and formation-sim, built on the probe, must run the real engine over in-memory partitions: B here, A there, the derived model says which.

Receipt 4 (stand-in-family-removed) turned green: the six hand-wired stand-ins and the cache SQL stand-in in membership-consistency-integration-test-helpers.js are replaced by hosts - CDC propagation on the deterministic virtual network with the real CDC owner on the leader node's clock and the cache owner's own apply at each follower (waitForPropagation runs the network; no wall-clock wait), a real unstarted MessageRouter (an unregistered peer is a disconnected peer), real TablePolicyService, ControlPlaneSystemTableGateway, ControlPlaneReadinessService, StorageCapacityAccountingService, StorageAdmissionService and RebalanceCoordinator wired the way ControlPlaneSetup wires them, and the ONE declared seam, the SQL engine: shape B with a contract (decision 2026-09-12) - test/query/sql-engine-system-table-contract-cases.js runs against the real SQLQueryEngine on a node booted the production way (test/integration/sql-engine-system-writes-contract.integration.test.js, 3/3) and against the seam (test/distributed/harness/__tests__/sql-engine-seam-conformance.test.js, 3/3); the registry pair sql-engine-cache-membership (contract sql-engine-system-table-read) declares harnessSeam {stub, contractCases, conformanceTest, realTest=the seven-node probe}; the model validates every pointer and the receipt seams-are-contract-bound is green. Quest probe: metric 0. The membership-consistency integration test itself now fails 7 of 14 subtests (50 pass / 15 fail) - see the finding that follows - so the quest cannot land until they are re-expressed or the fixture publishes membership.

Why seven membership subtests fail against the hosts (2, 3, 6, 7, 11, 13 and one orphaned subtest): the real UnifiedRebalancer.getAvailableNodes() returns getAvailableNodesConstrainedToNodeIds(publishedActiveNodeIds) and the real readiness owner's buildNodeReadinessSyncCurrent reads getPublicationDiagnostics/getMembershipPublicationDiagnosticsSync - a node is a member when it is in the PUBLISHED active set, not when its row exists in the nodes table. The stand-ins defined membership as row presence (createCacheBackedReadinessService decided ready from status/connection_state/lease on the raw row), and the seven subtests assert that definition ('rebalancer should see stale membership (1 node)': expected 1, got 0; 'lease sweep should process the expired node': expected [expiring-node], got []; 'leader should mark node as disconnected': the failure path never wrote through a published member; 'rebalancer1 should succeed': false). Verified the hosts' write path is sound (probe: insert/update succeed, propagation delivers on waitForPropagation; only 3 statements reached the seam all run because the subtests write rows straight into caches). Two honest resolutions, neither decided here: (a) the fixture publishes membership for its nodes through the real membership-publication owner (control_plane_publications rows / MembershipPublicationService), keeping the subtests' claims and letting 'CDC latency' act on publication propagation; (b) the subtests are re-expressed as claims about published membership under CDC latency, which is what the real owners define membership consistency to mean. Both keep the hosts; neither is a return to stand-ins.

The membership-consistency test's seven subtests encode the stand-ins' definition of membership (row presence) where the real owners define it as published membership; resolution (a) publish membership in the fixture through the real owner or (b) re-express the subtests against published membership is an owner judgment. Receipt 4 and the seam are complete; landing waits on this.

Owner decision (2026-09-12) on the membership subtests: (b) reached by (a)'s mechanism. The seven subtests are re-expressed as claims about PUBLISHED membership under CDC latency, and the fixture reaches the published state by driving the real publication owner on the real path, because that is the only production path to it. Rationale: the stand-ins did not merely drift, they defined membership as row presence; the real owners do not - a row in nodes is not a member until the publication owner publishes it and readiness reads it as published. Under (a) alone the assertions would keep the old vocabulary and pass only because the fixture quietly published first, carrying a hidden precondition. Under (b) the test says what the owners mean and gains a state the stand-ins could not express - row present, not yet published - the gap cold formation lives in (publication 5/5, the readiness lease, the membership-publication coordinator); that state gets a subtest of its own: an unpublished row is not a member on any node, and after publication it becomes one on every node within the latency bound. Conditions: (1) one-to-one - each of the seven is re-expressed against its original claim, with the original text kept here as the 'was'; (2) ruled-out beats rewritten - a claim that only made sense under row-presence semantics is deleted with a ruled-out finding, not massaged until it passes; (3) the fixture's publication step is the real owner on the real path, so 'CDC latency' means publication propagation, and the registered SQL-engine seam stays the only seam in the harness.

Fixture design for the seven re-expressions (facts established 2026-09-12, next sitting starts here). (1) In-process nodes booted by BootstrapService/NodeJoiningService share the NodeService singleton cache, so booted nodes cannot express per-node divergence; the composed per-cache hosts on the virtual network stay. (2) Subtests 3, 7, 11, 13 already boot a real seed and read NodeService.getInstance().getSystemTableCache(): on that seed the real publication owner publishes on the real path within seconds (observed row: publication_kind cluster_membership, status PUBLISHED, published_active_node_ids [seed], required/acknowledged acks). Their synthetic node rows are not published because the real coordinator admits only nodes it can witness (readiness lease, SWIM reachability through the router, acknowledgement); re-expressing them means their nodes must be admissible to the real owner - a real joiner in-process shares the cache, so admissibility must come through the owner's own inputs (published-set candidates, acks), which is the publication-acknowledgement path over the router. (3) Subtests 2, 6, 14 run on composed caches: publishing there needs the real local write chain - CDC owner local write -> partition -> committed-entry apply -> cache - which in production runs through the partition worker's CDCEmitter and the message-group replication apply (message-group-service-cdc-propagation-runtime-methods.applyCDCEvent, cdc-group-propagation-service.applyCDCEvent); the PartitionService itself takes a cdcIntegrationService but never calls it, so the in-process host must wire the emitter -> handler leg the message-group owner performs. (4) Leadership is live: tier 0 asks the CDC owner canWriteSystemTableLocally, which is true only with a local usable leader partition for control_plane_publications (a real single-replica PartitionService satisfies it honestly); the PARTITIONS/SERVICES tiers are fallbacks only when tier 0 is unavailable. (5) The SQL-engine seam contract covers the publication upsert (INSERT OR REPLACE by publication_id, owner status vocabulary), both legs 4/4. The one-to-one 'was' record: [2] rebalancer should see stale membership (1 node); rebalancer should see updated membership (2 nodes). [3] should have nodes available initially; short-lease node should not be available after lease expiry. [6] lease sweep should process the expired node; leader should mark node as disconnected; follower should see disconnected after CDC propagation. [7] both rebalancers should see same node count; should see at least seed node; rebalancer1/2 should succeed; should have moves array. [11] failing node visible in cache before detector runs; detector should see failing node before concurrent health check starts; insert operation for joining node; update operation for failing node; joining node should be in cache. [13] not stabilized immediately after state change; not stabilized after timer reset; time until stable reset to near full period. [14] cache1/cache2 should have 2 ready nodes; both caches should return same ready nodes.

Re-expression of the membership-consistency subtests against PUBLISHED membership, reached by driving the real publication owner on the real path (decision 2026-09-12; all 16 tests, 92 assertions green under the runner's TAP_TIMEOUT; direct node --test runs hit tap's 30 s file default, which the runner overrides from the file's {timeout} - the 'timeout!' on 13 and the orphaned 14 were that artefact, not membership). Fixture: (i) createReplicaPropagation - the follower leg is now the cache-change stream: every change the source cache applies is a virtual-network message applied at the follower through the cache owner's own apply, deliverUntil(predicate) delivers one committed change at a time (the stale window a lagging replica presents), and the source may be a booted seed's real cache; createCdcPropagationHost = that leg plus the real CDC owner on the leader clock (tests 1, 5 unchanged in claim). (ii) seedOwners(bootstrapService): the booted seed's REAL owners reached the way its runtime reaches them (readiness via the rebalance coordinator, publication coordinator via the heartbeat owner, gateway from the registry, lease and heartbeat owners). (iii) createNodeHosts now carries the real MembershipPublicationCoordinator wired into the readiness owner (the rebalancer reads published membership only through readiness.membershipPublicationService); leadership resolved honestly by isControlPlanePublicationsWriteLeader, so a composed node is a reader; the interval driver is not started. (iv) waitForPublishedMembership(cache, ids) reads the cache with the owners' own resolvePublishedActiveNodeIds; waitForPlacementEligible(readiness, id) drives the readiness owner's asynchronous evaluation until its synchronous verdict's dimensions.placementEligible holds. One-to-one record - [2] was 'rebalancer should see stale membership (1 node)' -> is 'no published membership while the publication is in flight (seed row present, not yet published)' + 'no member to place on before the publication'; was 'updated membership (2 nodes)' -> is 'rebalancer sees the published membership after propagation' ([seed], through its own getPublishedActiveNodeIdSet) + 'follower holds the seed publication'. Fixture: seed booted, follower replica subscribed BEFORE bootstrap, deliverUntil(seed node row). [3] was 'should have nodes available initially' -> is 'available nodes are the published set (the seed) while the short-lease row is present but unpublished'; was 'short-lease node should not be available after lease expiry' -> is 'an unpublished row stays unavailable after its lease expires: a member leaving on lease expiry is a republication by the publication owner, not a row read'. [6] moved from composed caches to the seed: the sweep reads the authoritative nodes table, which only an owner with a partition serves (composed host gateway answers owner_not_ready, rows []); was 'lease sweep should process the expired node', 'leader should mark node as disconnected', 'follower should see disconnected after CDC propagation' -> unchanged claims, now on the seed's real LeaseService (heartbeat owner performs the guarded disconnect) plus 'follower still sees ready before propagation'. [7] was 'should see at least seed node' -> is 'both rebalancers see the published set: the seed, not the unpublished node rows'; rebalance succeeds on both (real path, 1 move) - unchanged claims. [11] the spread-copy tracking wrapper (a stand-in that also made the detector build a gateway with no authority) is gone; was 'insert operation for joining node' -> is 'join write succeeds on the real path' + 'joining node is in the authoritative nodes table'; was 'update operation for failing node' -> is 'health check advanced the failing node past suspected' (authoritative read); 'failing node visible', 'detector sees failing node', 'joining node in cache', 'marked failed' unchanged. [5] the unused cdcUpdates spread wrapper removed; claims unchanged. Nothing ruled out: every claim found a published-membership expression on the real path.

Landing hygiene, no claim change: (1) the ambient-intrinsics guideline governs test/distributed/harness - the eleven direct prototype-method calls in owner-interaction-model.js (witnesses.includes) and its contract test (filter/flatMap/map/includes/startsWith chains) are captured at module load with Function.call.bind, the way the model module already captures its own; checker 0 violations over the whole governed scope, the contract test 5/5.
